title: Power Systems / Power Electronics
description: Power Systems / Power Electronics covers three-phase grids, network modeling, power flow, faults and protection, stability and renewables, plus converters, PWM, control, and motor/EV drives.

topics.title: Power System Fundamentals and Three-Phase Power
topics.description: Builds the language of electric power: why grids use sinusoidal three-phase quantities, how real/reactive/apparent power are interpreted, and how balanced and unbalanced operating conditions are represented.

children.title: Grid architecture and terminology
children.description: Students learn the basic roles of generation, transmission, substations, distribution feeders, loads, and interconnections so later calculations have a physical map.

children.title: Three-phase quantities
children.description: Three-phase analysis is the shorthand that makes large AC systems tractable and reveals how power is transferred efficiently.

children.title: Real, reactive, and apparent power
children.description: These quantities explain what energy is consumed, what energy oscillates through fields, and how equipment must be rated.

topics.title: Generation, Transmission, Distribution, and Loads
topics.description: Connects electrical calculations to the physical grid, from generating plants and renewable resources to transmission corridors, substations, feeders, and customer demand.

children.title: Generation technologies
children.description: Students compare how conventional, renewable, and storage-backed resources create electrical power and impose operating constraints.

children.title: Transmission and substation functions
children.description: Transmission equipment is studied as the high-voltage backbone that moves power while managing losses, voltage, and reliability.

children.title: Distribution and load behavior
children.description: Distribution systems show how end-use demand, feeder design, and load diversity shape the final delivery of power.

topics.title: Per-Unit System and Network Modeling
topics.description: Gives students the normalization and circuit-modeling tools used to compare equipment at different voltage levels without drowning in transformer ratios.

children.title: Base quantities
children.description: Per-unit notation turns voltage, current, impedance, and power into scaled values that are easier to compare across a system.

children.title: Single-line and impedance diagrams
children.description: Network diagrams reduce complex grids to analyzable models while preserving the relationships needed for calculations.

children.title: Admittance and bus models
children.description: Bus-admittance modeling prepares students for power-flow, fault, and simulation work.

topics.title: Transformers and Electric Machines
topics.description: Links magnetic energy conversion to grid operation and motor-drive applications, giving students the device-level intuition behind voltage conversion and electromechanical power.

children.title: Transformer principles
children.description: Transformers explain how voltage levels are changed, isolation is achieved, and impedance is reflected across windings.

children.title: Synchronous and induction machines
children.description: Machine models help students understand generators, motors, reactive power, and torque production.

children.title: Machines in converter-fed systems
children.description: Power electronics changes how machines are started, controlled, and protected in modern drives.

topics.title: Transmission Lines and Grid Components
topics.description: Develops the circuit models for lines, cables, breakers, capacitors, reactors, and compensating devices that determine voltage, loading, and losses.

children.title: Line parameters
children.description: Students learn how resistance, inductance, capacitance, and conductance arise from physical line construction.

children.title: Voltage regulation and losses
children.description: Line models are used to predict receiving-end voltage, power transfer limits, and efficiency.

children.title: Compensation equipment
children.description: Reactive and flexible AC devices are introduced as tools for voltage support and transfer capability.

topics.title: Power Flow Analysis and Newton-Raphson Methods
topics.description: Shows how engineers solve for bus voltages, angles, line flows, and losses under normal operating conditions, using the same concepts embedded in industry software.

children.title: Power-flow problem setup
children.description: Students define buses, loads, generation, and constraints so the network equations match the operating question.

children.title: Gauss-Seidel and Newton-Raphson methods
children.description: Iterative methods translate nonlinear AC power equations into solvable numerical workflows.

children.title: Interpreting results
children.description: Power-flow output becomes actionable when students can diagnose overloads, voltage problems, and sensitivity to changes.

topics.title: Fault Analysis, Symmetrical Components, and Protection
topics.description: Prepares students to calculate short-circuit currents and understand how protective devices isolate faults without unnecessary service interruption.

children.title: Symmetrical faults
children.description: Balanced three-phase faults establish the baseline for short-circuit current magnitude and equipment duty.

children.title: Symmetrical components
children.description: Sequence networks make unbalanced faults analyzable by decomposing them into positive, negative, and zero-sequence systems.

children.title: Protection and relaying
children.description: Protection converts fault analysis into settings and coordination decisions that keep people and equipment safe.

topics.title: Power System Stability, Voltage/Frequency Control, and Operations
topics.description: Extends beyond steady-state calculations into how the grid survives disturbances, balances supply and demand, and maintains usable voltage and frequency.

children.title: Rotor angle, voltage, and frequency stability
children.description: Stability concepts explain why a mathematically feasible operating point still may not survive a disturbance.

children.title: Economic dispatch and operation
children.description: Dispatch introduces the optimization and operational constraints behind real-time generation scheduling.

children.title: Control mechanisms
children.description: Students connect control loops and grid equipment to frequency, voltage, and power-sharing objectives.

topics.title: Renewable Integration, Energy Storage, Smart Grids, and Resilience
topics.description: Places classical power engineering into the modern grid, where inverter-based resources, storage, digital controls, reliability, and resilience are central design concerns.

children.title: Renewable and inverter-based resources
children.description: Students learn why wind, solar, and converter-interfaced generation change fault current, inertia, voltage support, and control behavior.

children.title: Energy storage and demand flexibility
children.description: Storage and flexible loads are treated as operating tools for balancing, peak reduction, and resilience.

children.title: Smart-grid resilience
children.description: Digital monitoring and automation are introduced alongside reliability and recovery objectives.

topics.title: Power Semiconductor Devices and Gate Drives
topics.description: Introduces the switching devices that make modern conversion possible and the driver circuits that turn ideal switching diagrams into working hardware.

children.title: Power semiconductor families
children.description: Students compare devices by voltage, current, switching speed, conduction loss, and application domain.

children.title: Switching behavior and losses
children.description: Switching is studied as a nonideal process that sets efficiency, thermal stress, and electromagnetic noise.

children.title: Gate-drive requirements
children.description: Gate drives provide the interface between control signals and high-energy switches.

topics.title: Power Electronic Converter Topologies
topics.description: Builds the converter vocabulary students need for regulated DC supplies, renewable interfaces, motor drives, and grid-connected systems.

children.title: DC-DC converters
children.description: Basic chopper circuits show how switching and energy storage regulate DC voltage and current.

children.title: Isolated converters
children.description: Isolation and high-frequency transformers expand converter design for safety, voltage scaling, and power density.

children.title: Converter performance metrics
children.description: Topology choice is tied to efficiency, ripple, device stress, control complexity, and application fit.

topics.title: Rectifiers, Inverters, PWM, and Harmonics
topics.description: Covers conversion between AC and DC and the modulation techniques that shape output voltage, current quality, and harmonic content.

children.title: Rectifiers and AC-DC conversion
children.description: Students learn how diode and controlled rectifiers produce DC from AC while affecting source currents and power quality.

children.title: Inverters and DC-AC conversion
children.description: Inverters are studied as the foundation for motor drives, grid-tied renewables, UPS systems, and AC power supplies.

children.title: PWM and harmonic analysis
children.description: Modulation explains how switching patterns determine fundamental output, harmonics, filtering needs, and losses.

topics.title: Converter Control, Magnetics, Thermal Design, EMI, and Safety
topics.description: Turns converter circuits into engineered systems by addressing regulation, passive components, heat removal, electromagnetic compatibility, and safe operation.

children.title: Feedback control of converters
children.description: Closed-loop control keeps voltage, current, or power regulated under load and input disturbances.

children.title: Magnetics and passive components
children.description: Inductors, transformers, and capacitors determine ripple, energy storage, size, cost, and reliability.

children.title: Thermal, EMI, and safety design
children.description: High-power switching hardware must manage heat, noise, isolation, creepage, clearance, and standards constraints.

topics.title: Motor Drives, EV Powertrains, and Applications
topics.description: Applies power electronics to motion, electrified transportation, renewable systems, and industrial power conversion.

children.title: Motor drive architecture
children.description: Students connect converters, sensors, control loops, machines, and mechanical loads into a complete drive system.

children.title: EV and battery-charging systems
children.description: Transportation applications show how conversion, storage, thermal limits, safety, and controls interact in a high-impact domain.

children.title: Application integration
children.description: Students close the course by matching power-system and converter choices to practical engineering use cases.
